 Republican Rep. Randy Fine wins re-election in Florida’s 6th Congressional District 
 Florida News 
 By Michelle Vecerina 
 Published Nov. 3, 2026, 7:29 p.m. ET | Updated Nov. 3, 2026
 U.S. Rep. Randy Fine. (Photo/Congress website) 
 DAYTONA BEACH, Fla. — Republican U.S. Rep. Randy Fine has secured his first full term in Congress, defeating Democratic challenger Eric Yonce to retain Florida’s 6th Congressional District for the GOP.
 Fine, who took office in April 2025 after winning a special election to succeed former Rep. Mike Waltz, campaigned on an “America First” platform prioritizing border enforcement, cuts to federal spending, energy independence and opposition to federal regulatory mandates.
 Throughout the race, Fine highlighted his voting record in Washington as well as his prior tenure in the Florida Legislature. During eight years in Tallahassee, Fine played a central role in high-profile conservative legislative battles, sponsoring state measures to restrict Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion, or DEI spending in higher education, authoring Florida’s statutory definition of antisemitism, expanding school choice voucher programs, and leading the effort to dissolve special tax districts for corporate entities.
 In Congress, Fine joined the House Freedom Caucus and served on the House Foreign Affairs and Education and Workforce committees, frequently taking a hard line on national security, foreign aid oversight, and federal education policy.
 Yonce, a Democrat who ran in the Republican-leaning district that spans Flagler, Volusia, Marion, Putnam, Lake, and St. Johns counties, focused his campaign on healthcare access, local infrastructure investments, and cost-of-living relief. However, Yonce faced substantial headwinds in overcoming Fine’s fundraising edge, district-wide name recognition and Republican voter registration across the region.
 Fine’s re-election keeps Florida’s 6th District firmly in Republican hands, giving the incumbent another term for the vocal conservative lawmaker in Florida’s federal delegation.
